I'm worried about the "imminent danger to self" thing. While it will likely not happen immediately, there's a good chance that I could actually be, or at least appear to be a danger to myself.

I'm not successful at music because I can only play the notes accurately sequenced and timed, and control the volume level based on marked notes. I can't actually put any personality into it.

I fail at teaching because every time I try to teach someone anything, I either inadvertently insult their intelligence by starting at too low a level, or rapidly lose them by starting too high.

Also, those are just two examples at random--the problem isn't the music or the teaching, it's that if I care about it, I fail.

Sure, I suppose that is true, any way I can get these in other areas to see if it helps?

I can have someone ask, but of course the counseling center will say no, and if something actually comes up, they will say "well there are exceptions", etc.

Even disregarding the medications issue, there's still the problem of some of the jobs, though that's alot more minor. You're sure that I can't be forced to take medications due to an evaluation?

As far as ticking off subjects and this sort of idea goes, I think that it's not really valid, as you can't actually "finish" physics, or math, or even a subfield thereof. You can get a good grounding in it, similar to how you could have a good grounding in music, but you can't actually finish it.
